title: The “super influencers” powering the post-Trump right | Institute for Family Studies
gist: A short excerpt (from Vox, republished by IFS) reports that commentator Aaron Renn has been labeled the No. 1 'intellectual super influencer' for a major swath of the Trump-era right, treating himself as validated by the ranking.

themes.theme: Intellectual Influence Rankings on the New Right

insights.claim: Commentator Aaron Renn was labeled by Vox's reporting as the No. 1 'intellectual super influencer' for a major swath of the Trump-era political right, indicating an emerging effort to formally map and rank ideological influence networks within that movement.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: The existence of a formal 'super influencer' ranking for the New Right suggests growing media/analyst interest in quantifying ideological influence networks — relevant for anyone tracking which commentators shape policy and cultural narratives feeding into IFS-adjacent family/tech policy debates.
insights.locator: It’s not every day that you get labeled the No. 1 “intellectual super influencer”

insights.claim: Renn's own reaction — welcoming the ranking as 'independent validation' of his work — illustrates how New Right intellectuals treat media-generated influence rankings as a legitimizing credential rather than dismissing them.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: A small but telling data point on how ideological influencers self-market and use third-party media coverage to build authority within their movement.
insights.quote: It’s always good to have some independent validation of your work
insights.locator: Aaron Renn was in a good mood
